All at the head sha above (REST contents reads); the one local-checkout grep is named where it is cited.

Inputs: card objectui#12099 (body and all four comments, the os-dev report `6215866081` included), ruling C on objectstack-ai/objectstack#22444 comment `6100463199`, the PR body, file list and net diff against `main` at the head, the head's check-runs, objectui#12670 and objectui#12649. The brief's own conclusions were not adopted; each item below was re-read in the cited code.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Registration `inputs` / `defaultProps`, measured on what `@object-ui/plugin-list` publishes — RIGHT.** `package.json` publishes one entry (`.` → `dist/index.js`, `dist/index.umd.cjs`, `dist/index.d.ts`) and `files` = `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`. The built entry's export list (`src/index.tsx`: `ListView`, `ListViewBlock`, `ViewSwitcher`, `ObjectGallery`, `ViewSwitcherDropdown`, `TabBar`, `TabBarSelect`, `UserFilters`, the three normalizers, `LIST_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS`, the prop and handle types) is unchanged by the diff. Every new symbol in `ListViewBlock.tsx` (`toListViewHandOff`, `namesRecordSource`, `ListViewNoObjectHint`, `PageNodeBag`, `RETIRED_PAGE_KEYS`, the warn set) is module-private, and `ListViewBlock`'s declared shape (`elementDataSourceBlock` over a `forwardRef` of `ListViewHandle` / `ListViewProps`) is as before, so the `.d.ts` closure does not move; the dev's reading (10 `dist/*.d.ts` byte-identical) is consistent with what the source exports. The contract moves in the registration side effect `dist/index.js` carries: on both `list-view` and `view:list`, inputs `objectName` + `viewType` become `data` (type `object`, the spec's `ViewData`) + `type` (enum of the nine kinds, not required); `list-view`'s `defaultProps` `{ objectName: '', viewType: 'grid', … }` become `{ data: { provider: 'object', object: '' }, columns: [], filter: [], sort: [], options: {} }`. The README, in `files`, publishes with it. Pinned through the real registry in the new test's last `describe`.

2. **A page node in the old spelling at render — RIGHT, and no fallback read remains on the page path.** `toListViewHandOff` runs before the gate: a node whose top-level `objectName` or `viewType` is `!== undefined` (the old default `objectName: ''` included) has both keys removed, and `console.warn` names the key and the remedy once per key per process. The hoist has already flattened `properties.objectName` / `properties.viewType` onto the node, so bag and flat are one case. A node whose only object is the retired key therefore names none: `namesRecordSource`, judged inside the gate's render-prop after the binding applied, draws the `list-view-no-object` panel with the gate's own `view.noObject` key and `property: 'data.object'`, and `ListView` is never mounted, so nothing is fetched. Read for a remaining read: `SchemaRenderer.tsx` at head has zero `objectName` / `viewType` reads; `useElementDataSource.ts` has none live (its one mention is a doc comment); the gate WRITES them (`next[objectKey] = composed.object` unconditionally; `next.viewType` only when `base.viewType === undefined`); `ListView.tsx` reads only the hand-off schema (no `props.objectName`, no read of `schema.properties`); the retained `properties` bag is read by the block for `type` alone. The ruling's clause (stored nodes are carried by the spec's ADR-0087 D2 conversion, never a fallback read here) holds on this tree. Pinned in the new file (bag and flat, the warning count, the `viewType`-beside-`data` control) and the console `objectname-neither-hint-11605` rows.

3. **How `properties.type` reaches the list without clobbering the node's `type` — RIGHT.** `HOIST_PROTECTED_KEYS = new Set(['type', 'id'])` is untouched; the memo's hoist skips `type` and `id`, restores `outerType` / `outerId`, and keeps `newSchema.properties = props` on the node. So the block's narrow read — `isConfigBag(bag) ? bag.type : undefined`, then `isListViewVisualization(kind)` from `@object-ui/core` — is the only channel; a non-kind (`'page'`, or the registry key itself) is dropped and the list is a grid. Chosen over a global hoist change that would have reached `page:tabs` and `element:metadata_viewer`, whose spec `type` members mean something else: the right narrowness. Pinned: the kanban spy receives the `object-kanban` node `ListView` builds and no "Unknown component" is drawn.

4. **A node-stated kind over a bound saved view's kind — RIGHT.** The block writes `viewType` from `properties.type` before the gate; the gate's `viewType` branch only fills absence; absent, `normalizeListViewSchema` resolves `authoredViewKind ?? 'grid'`. So node kind outranks view kind, view kind applies when the node states none, grid otherwise — the README's standing rule (the component's key wins, `filter` excepted), now stated for the kind. Pinned three ways in the new file and re-spelled in `ListView.sharedGate`. The dev's out-of-scope note that the react tier's `specType` has the opposite precedence is a pre-existing read of another carrier, not this diff's.

5. **The html tier — RIGHT, as ruling C's consequence.** `parse.ts` refuses a `type` attribute at parse (`DISCRIMINATOR_ATTR = 'type'`, the existing `forbidden-attr` code: the tag is the component), and `properties` is not in `SDUI_BASE_PROPS`, so no attribute on that tier can state the list kind once `viewType` is gone: an html list-view tag draws a non-grid kind only through `dataSource.view`, and `viewType=` / `objectName=` now draw `unknown-prop` (pinned in `objectname-binding-required-11605`). `data` is both a declared input and a where-undeclared base prop, so `data={{ provider: 'object', object }}` compiles with zero diagnostics (pinned). Ruling C refused a carrier-specific envelope (its option B); an html-only kind attribute would be exactly that, so the loss is what C accepts.

6. **The dev's deviations.**
   - `defaultProps` publish `data` but no `type` — RIGHT. Absence is the spec's own grid default and is what lets a bound saved view's kind apply; a `type: 'grid'` default would collide with the registry key in any consumer that spreads defaults onto a node (the designer's palette path stores a palette item's `defaultProps` as the node's `props` bag). The `type` input is published; the ruling's words ("publishes `data` / `type` instead") name the spelling, not a default value; the card's intent (new spelling in, old spelling out of both inputs and defaults) is met.
   - The gate still lands `dataSource.object` on `objectName` — RIGHT. That key is the hand-off between the gate and the `ListView` component's props (which still spell `objectName` / `viewType`; see ③), never a read of the page node, whose own keys are gone before the gate runs. `normalizeListViewSchema`'s `data` → `objectName` fold is gap-fill only (a non-empty `objectName` wins), so a bound object survives the registration's empty `data.object` default and outranks an authored `data.object`, as the guide now says. Landing the binding into `data` would overwrite an authored rows / `value`-provider `data` or need a new gate option in `@object-ui/react` outside the claim.

Also read, not WRONG: `toListViewHandOff` reads `properties` only; the legacy `props` alias bag's `type` is never hoisted and is not read, which matches the ruling's own wording (`properties.type`). A grep of non-test `type: 'list-view'` literals in the local objectui checkout at `8614705c` finds the four sites the dev's census names (plugin-view `ObjectView.tsx`, app-shell `InterfaceListPage.tsx` and `ObjectDataPage.tsx`, a doc comment in `objectql.zod.ts`), each a `ListView` component schema, none a page node; the ruling's "seven files" counted README and guides. `view.noObject` carries `{{property}}` in the locale packs; `check:i18n-keys` is inside the green Repo Gates.

**Check-runs on the head (36):** 32 success — `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Repo Gates`, `Build & E2E`, `Test (shard 1/16 … 16/16)`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Test`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `label`; 3 skipped — `Test (coverage)`, the coverage shard matrix, `dependabot`; 1 failure — `Live E2E (informational)`. Nothing in_progress at the last read: `Test (shard 3/16)` was in_progress at my first read and completed success 2026-10-16T12:57Z. On the red: its job log is not readable from this container (the log blob answers Forbidden through the proxy); its annotations are "No files were found with the provided path: test-results/, backend.log, console-preview.log" and "Process completed with exit code 1" — no spec ran and no artifact was uploaded, the shape objectui#12649 names (a cold live-backend `npm install` dying in arborist). This PR touches no `e2e/**` path. Read as the lane's standing red, not this PR's.

### ② Semver level

- **`@object-ui/plugin-list: minor` with the break in prose — RIGHT, the repo's correct spelling.** objectui AGENTS.md §9 (版本号策略): the fixed group's major tracks `@objectstack`'s, and 「changeset 里不要声明 `major` …… objectui 自身的破坏性变更也标 `minor`(在正文里写清 breaking 语义即可)」, enforced by `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (`Changeset Bump Policy`: success). The body carries the FROM → TO mapping (`objectName` → `data: { provider: 'object', object }`, `viewType` → `properties.type`), the runtime symptom (the hint naming `data.object`, one warning per key), who converts stored nodes (the spec's ADR-0087 conversion), and that `ListViewSchema`'s React props are unchanged. The fixed group (`.changeset/config.json`, `plugin-list` among its members) takes the minor together.
- **The PR body's `Clause-②:` line against the diff — WRONG as spelled, right in substance; a body correction before ready, not a re-review.** The diff widens (publishes `data` / `type`, reads `properties.type`) and narrows (retires `objectName` / `viewType` from the inputs and from every page read — the changeset's own "Breaking" bullet). The declaration is `yes|no` plus at most one arm of the closed pair `(widening)` / `(narrowing)`; `(narrowing)` is the arm with a consequence, since it is what makes a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review owed, and `yes (widening, with the old spelling retired)` is not a closed-pair spelling. Measured: `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths` over this file list says the paths decide no face and the `Clause-②:` line decides; read against this line it finds no `(narrowing)` arm and would route the PR to the declaration face (`TIER_DEFAULT`), under-stating the review owed. None of objectui's four changeset gates parses the arm (they judge structure), so nothing mechanical reds it. This record serves the higher tier regardless; the body's line should read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — the widening half is already carried by `yes` → `minor`. The changeset body carries no `Clause-②:` line and objectui's rules do not ask for one there.
